key_insight: The paper asks when an open model can reliably stand in for a closed-model API in interpretability studies. It shows that surrogate fidelity depends on the level of analysis—prediction, attribution, or representation—rather than assuming open models are always good proxies.
problem_solved: Mechanistic interpretability usually needs full access to model internals, but most deployed LLMs only expose limited outputs like token log-probabilities. This paper addresses the surrogate problem: when measurements from open models can support valid claims about closed models.
method: Evaluate surrogate fidelity at three levels: prediction, attribution, and representation.
Use binary classification tasks to study whether API-accessible log-odds can serve as a faithful readout of model behavior.
Compare open-model measurements against closed-model targets to identify where surrogate assumptions hold or break.
impact: This work gives researchers a framework for knowing when open models are reliable stand-ins for proprietary LLMs. That can make interpretability claims more rigorous and reduce the risk of drawing incorrect conclusions from surrogate analyses.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of open model vs. closed model with an API boundary in between.
Three-layer pipeline showing prediction, attribution, and representation fidelity.
Binary classification chart mapping log-odds to model outputs.
Fidelity heatmap or traffic-light indicator showing where surrogate agreement is strong or weak.
paper_title: Surrogate Fidelity: When Can Open LLMs Explain Closed Ones?
paper_authors: Philippe Chlenski, Zachariah Carmichael, Ayush Warikoo, Chia-Tse Shao, Yingxiao Ye
